scope: 77 bounded primary-source assessments: complete legacy 30-product and current FDA 20-product inherited gene-therapy inventories, with EU additions and representative RNA, enzyme/protein replacement, antibody bypass, hormone, chaperone, substrate-reduction, stabilizer, CFTR and tissue comparators. Trial outcomes, regional indications, variant eligibility, human engagement and cell-rescue uncertainty stay separate. Not every approved inherited-disease medicine or every indication is curated; explicit remaining gaps are recorded.

trials.name: ENDEAR
trials.summary: Sham-controlled trial: motor milestone response in 37/73 treated infants versus 0/37 controls at final analysis; death/permanent-ventilation hazard ratio 0.53.

phenotypes.label: Delayed gross motor development
phenotypes.rationale: Motor milestones assess gross motor development; they do not measure global cognitive development.

phenotypes.label: Respiratory insufficiency
phenotypes.rationale: A composite of survival and ventilation; not a direct measurement of every respiratory symptom.

exposed: Central nervous system after intrathecal dosing
engaged: SMN2 splicing; cell-subtype specificity unresolved
cells.notes: SMN restoration is supported. Clinical endpoints do not isolate the contribution of motor neurons from other exposed cells.

evidence.claim: Nusinersen increases SMN2 exon 7 inclusion and full-length SMN protein; this compensates for SMN1 deficiency.
Randomized motor and survival outcomes support the SMN-restoration strategy.
The clinical trial did not compare cell-restricted delivery, so benefit cannot establish a unique causal cell type.

conclusion.summary: Supports SMN restoration and motor benefit; does not independently validate a specific atlas cell-type prediction.

limitations: The disease gene and therapeutic splice target differ.
Disease duration affects response; an absent later response need not refute motor-neuron involvement.
assessments.geneRoleNotes: SMN1 deficiency causes 5q SMA; SMN2 pre-mRNA is the therapeutic splice target.

regulatory.status: Approved; viable retinal cells required

trials.name: Pivotal phase 3
trials.summary: Randomized open-label trial with masked mobility graders: one-year bilateral mobility change difference 1.6 light levels (95% CI 0.72–2.41).

phenotypes.label: Visual impairment
phenotypes.endpoint: Multi-luminance mobility test at one year
phenotypes.rationale: Functional vision under varying light conditions is measured; this is not the same endpoint as visual acuity.

diseaseRelevant: Photoreceptors supported by the visual cycle
engaged: Retinal pigment epithelial cells: RPE65 expression
bypass: Photoreceptors benefit through restored visual-cycle support
cells.notes: RPE is the transduced compartment. Photoreceptor involvement is compatible with benefit through an adjacent supporting cell.

evidence.claim: The label describes RPE-cell transduction and restoration of the retinoid cycle.
Controlled functional-vision improvement connects local retinal treatment to the measured phenotype.
A photoreceptor atlas association would not mean photoreceptors were directly transduced; the treatment acts through RPE support.

conclusion.summary: Convergent evidence supports RPE-mediated visual rescue; it does not make every visual phenotype or retinal cell subtype a validated target.

limitations: Viable retina is a treatment prerequisite.
Small trial; treatment and participants were not masked.

regulatory.status: US accelerated approval November 2024; EU authorization under exceptional circumstances July 2022 for severe genetically confirmed AADC deficiency from 18 months

trials.name: AADC-002 / FDA Study 1
trials.summary: Single-arm study with external natural history comparison: 8/12 assessed patients acquired a new gross motor milestone at week 48.

trials.name: AADC-CU/1601 and AADC-010 (EMA review)
trials.summary: Single-arm cohorts acquired and maintained motor milestones; follow-up was incomplete and varying by time point. These are distinct cohorts from FDA Study 1.

phenotypes.label: Delayed gross motor development
phenotypes.endpoint: PDMS-2 gross motor milestones at week 48
phenotypes.rationale: Motor milestones were measured directly. Post-treatment dyskinesia is a safety finding, not proof of dystonia improvement.

diseaseRelevant: Monoaminergic systems affected by AADC deficiency
engaged: Putamen: increased AADC-associated PET signal and CSF dopamine metabolite
bypass: Local dopamine production may restore circuit function
cells.notes: Regional delivery and PET do not establish the identity of every transduced neuron or rescue of the original monoaminergic cell population.

evidence.claim: Putamen AADC activity and CSF homovanillic acid increased after treatment.
New gross motor milestones support functional benefit in the studied children.
Dyskinesia was an adverse reaction; it must not be converted into an efficacy endpoint for dystonia.

conclusion.summary: Supports regional neurotransmitter restoration and motor benefit; cell-subtype causality remains unresolved.

limitations: External controls cannot provide all protections of randomization.
Accelerated approval requires verification and durability evidence.
FDA pivotal trial differs from older Upstaza studies; do not count the brands as independent mechanistic replications.

regulatory.status: Approved for adult hATTR polyneuropathy

trials.name: APOLLO
trials.summary: Randomized placebo-controlled study of 225 participants: 18-month mNIS+7 change −6.0 versus +28.0; between-group difference −34.0 points.

phenotypes.label: Peripheral neuropathy
phenotypes.endpoint: Modified Neuropathy Impairment Score +7 at 18 months
phenotypes.rationale: A composite neuropathy assessment; does not isolate a particular peripheral neural cell subtype.

engaged: Hepatocytes: TTR mRNA cleavage
bypass: Peripheral nerves benefit from reduced circulating amyloid precursor
cells.notes: The principal drug-delivery compartment and the clinically injured compartment differ.

evidence.claim: The siRNA formulation delivers to hepatocytes and reduces mutant and wild-type TTR production.
APOLLO demonstrated improved neuropathy compared with placebo.
These data oppose treating neuropathy benefit as proof of direct neuronal or Schwann-cell drug engagement; hepatic precursor reduction is the documented mechanism.

conclusion.summary: Clinical rescue can occur through the liver without direct treatment of the predicted neural cell. This is a non-cell-autonomous mechanism, not a failed neural hypothesis.

limitations: Do not score a therapeutic-cell mismatch as evidence that the disease-relevant cell is wrong.
This row addresses polyneuropathy, not every cardiac or ocular manifestation.

assessments.disease: Sickle cell disease with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises; transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia
assessments.modality: Ex vivo CRISPR editing of autologous hematopoietic progenitors

regulatory.status: Approved for SCD with recurrent VOCs and TDT at age 2 years and older (July 2026 label, STN 125787).

trials.name: CLIMB SCD-121
trials.summary: CLIMB SCD-121 publication: 29/30 evaluable participants were free of severe VOCs for at least 12 consecutive months; 44 treated. FDA label includes an additional early nonresponder: 29/31 (93.5%).

trials.name: CLIMB THAL-111
trials.summary: 52 treated; 32/35 evaluable patients achieved at least 12 consecutive months without RBC transfusion while maintaining weighted mean hemoglobin at least 9 g/dL.

trials.name: CLIMB SCD-151 / Trial 4
trials.summary: Age 5–11 years: 11 treated; all 8 efficacy-evaluable patients achieved 12-month severe-VOC freedom.

trials.name: CLIMB THAL-141 / Trial 5
trials.summary: Age 5–11 years: 15 treated; 8/9 efficacy-evaluable achieved transfusion independence; denominator includes a patient who died from veno-occlusive disease.

phenotypes.label: Pain
phenotypes.endpoint: Freedom from protocol-defined severe vaso-occlusive crises
phenotypes.rationale: Vaso-occlusive crises include a defined clinical event set. Broad pain is an imperfect HPO crosswalk, not a separately measured pain subtype.

phenotypes.label: Anemia
phenotypes.endpoint: Transfusion independence with sustained hemoglobin threshold
phenotypes.rationale: Transfusion independence is a treatment-requirement endpoint, not a complete measurement of every anemia manifestation.

exposed: Autologous CD34+ hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells ex vivo
engaged: Edited progenitors and erythroid descendants: increased fetal hemoglobin
rescue: Erythroid descendants: fetal hemoglobin compensates for deficient or sickling beta-globin
cells.notes: Administered stem cells, molecularly regulated erythroid cells and mature red-cell effectors are distinct stages of one lineage.

evidence.claim: Editing the erythroid-specific BCL11A enhancer increases fetal hemoglobin in erythroid descendants.
The trial observed sustained freedom from severe vaso-occlusive events in most evaluable participants.
The strategy compensates for HBB disease through another locus; it does not repair each HBB variant or validate a generic pain-associated cell.
The separate thalassemia trial supports erythroid compensation and sustained transfusion independence.

conclusion.summary: Supports erythroid compensation in SCD and TDT; pain associations remain a broad clinical proxy.

limitations: Single-arm study and evaluability subset require separate denominators.
Conditioning and transplantation add risks not represented by target compatibility.
A source population age range is not the current regulatory indication.
Age 2–4 approval is extrapolated; clinical trials did not study children younger than 5 years.
assessments.geneRoleNotes: HBB is the disease gene; the erythroid BCL11A enhancer is edited to derepress fetal globin.

assessments.modality: Ex vivo lentiviral hematopoietic stem-cell gene augmentation

regulatory.status: Approved for specified presymptomatic or early-symptomatic pediatric subgroups

trials.name: ARSA gene therapy phase 1/2 and expanded access
trials.summary: Nonrandomized treated cohort compared with natural history showed preservation of motor and cognitive function, particularly with early treatment.

phenotypes.label: Gait disturbance
phenotypes.endpoint: Gross Motor Function Measure and severe motor impairment-free survival
phenotypes.rationale: Motor preservation includes ambulation and sitting; it does not directly quantify every gait abnormality.

diseaseRelevant: Myelinating cells and neural tissues affected by sulfatide accumulation
exposed: Autologous CD34+ hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells ex vivo
engaged: Hematopoietic descendants: ARSA activity
bypass: ARSA-producing progeny supply enzyme to affected tissues
cells.notes: Blood enzyme activity confirms hematopoietic pharmacodynamics, not cell-specific correction of every oligodendrocyte or Schwann cell.

evidence.claim: Transduced hematopoietic stem cells and progeny produce functional ARSA; peripheral blood activity is a pharmacodynamic measure.
Motor and cognitive outcomes support early intervention in the studied MLD populations.
The cited clinical evidence does not resolve which recipient neural cell populations mediate each rescued phenotype.

conclusion.summary: Supports enzyme supply through a hematopoietic route; does not require the transduced cell to equal the disease-injured cell.

limitations: Disease stage strongly limits generalization.
Natural-history comparison is not randomized.
Lenmeldy and Libmeldy represent the same active therapy, not independent validations.

regulatory.status: Approved to slow loss of ambulation in pediatric CLN2 disease

trials.name: CLN2 pivotal study
trials.summary: Open-label intraventricular enzyme treatment slowed motor-language decline compared with historical controls.

phenotypes.label: Gait disturbance
phenotypes.rationale: Loss of ambulation is within the motor phenotype domain, but the trial scale is not an exact HPO gait measure.

diseaseRelevant: Central nervous system cells affected by TPP1 deficiency
engaged: CNS lysosomes via mannose-6-phosphate receptor uptake
cells.notes: The receptor-mediated mechanism is not restricted to one neuronal subtype; clinical motor preservation is not cell-restricted rescue.

evidence.claim: Cerliponase alfa is taken up into CNS-cell lysosomes through the cation-independent mannose-6-phosphate receptor.
Motor-language decline was slower than in historical controls.
The comparative clinical outcome does not identify one uniquely causal or rescued CNS cell subtype.

conclusion.summary: Supports CNS enzyme replacement and motor preservation; fine cell-type validation is unresolved.

limitations: Historical-control comparison.
Intraventricular delivery and device complications are material treatment constraints.

assessments.disease: Cystic fibrosis with an ivacaftor-responsive CFTR variant

regulatory.status: Approved for specified responsive variants

trials.name: STRIVE / VX08-770-102
trials.summary: Randomized G551D trial demonstrated improvement in percent-predicted FEV1 compared with placebo.

phenotypes.label: Reduced forced expiratory volume in one second
phenotypes.rationale: The endpoint measures the named physiological phenotype; this HPO term may lack an atlas prediction.

exposed: CFTR-bearing epithelial cells; specific in vivo subtype unresolved
engaged: CFTR channel gating in patient-derived bronchial epithelial cultures
rescue: Bronchial epithelial chloride transport in vitro
cells.notes: Epithelial mechanism is supported, but a trial does not identify which airway epithelial subtype is necessary or sufficient.

evidence.claim: Ivacaftor increases chloride transport in patient-derived bronchial epithelial cultures carrying responsive variants.
Randomized lung-function benefit connects CFTR modulation to a respiratory endpoint.
Response depends on membrane-localized CFTR and variant responsiveness; neither all missense variants nor all CFTR loss-of-function alleles qualify.

conclusion.summary: Supports an airway epithelial CFTR mechanism; variant-specific response evidence remains essential.

limitations: Gene-level membership alone is insufficient for eligibility.
Magnitude of in vitro chloride rescue does not directly predict individual clinical effect.

regulatory.status: Accelerated approval based on plasma neurofilament light reduction

trials.name: VALOR randomized phase
trials.summary: The prespecified 28-week ALSFRS-R primary endpoint was not statistically significant, despite biomarker reductions.

trials.name: VALOR open-label extension
trials.summary: Longer follow-up associated earlier initiation with numerically less functional decline; crossover, attrition and limited power constrain the comparison.

phenotypes.label: Muscle weakness
phenotypes.endpoint: ALSFRS-R clinical function; separate NfL biomarker
phenotypes.rationale: ALSFRS-R is multidomain; NfL is an injury biomarker, not a direct muscle-strength or cell-rescue endpoint.

exposed: Residual human motor neurons in autopsy samples
engaged: Residual motor neurons: low SOD1 mRNA signal; spinal tissue SOD1 reduction
cells.notes: Human tissue confirms exposure and molecular engagement. It does not establish survival or functional rescue of the same neurons.

evidence.claim: A 2026 autopsy series found tofersen in residual motor neurons with low SOD1 mRNA signal; three recently treated donors had 45–84% lumbar tissue SOD1 mRNA/protein reductions.
The randomized 28-week primary clinical analysis did not establish benefit on ALSFRS-R.
The longer early-start versus delayed-start comparison is compatible with clinical benefit but does not preserve a long-term untreated randomized control.
Autopsy selection and persistent misfolded SOD1 inclusions preclude equating molecular engagement with complete cellular rescue.

conclusion.summary: Direct human motor-neuron engagement is demonstrated; clinical evidence varies by timepoint and study design, and the pivotal endpoint was null.

limitations: Keep accelerated approval, NfL response, clinical outcomes and tissue engagement separate.
Autopsy series is small and selected.
A null short-duration endpoint alone does not refute motor-neuron causality.

assessments.disease: Duchenne muscular dystrophy with exon-51-skipping-amenable variants

regulatory.status: Accelerated approval based on skeletal-muscle dystrophin increase

trials.name: Study 201 / FDA Study 1
trials.summary: Small placebo-controlled study with crossover investigated dystrophin and walking distance; the label states clinical benefit was not established and its external-control Study 2 did not show benefit.

phenotypes.label: Muscle weakness
phenotypes.rationale: Dystrophin is molecular engagement; walking is functional but is not an isolated muscle-strength measurement.

engaged: Skeletal-muscle dystrophin production
cells.notes: Biopsy protein production is engagement evidence. It does not by itself demonstrate meaningful phenotypic rescue.

evidence.claim: Exon 51 skipping can restore the reading frame for specific DMD genotypes and produce a shortened dystrophin.
Increased skeletal-muscle dystrophin supported accelerated approval.
The cited label distinguishes molecular dystrophin production from unestablished clinical benefit.

conclusion.summary: Muscle engagement is supported, but a clinically rescued phenotype cannot be asserted from the approval surrogate alone.

limitations: Amenability depends on exact exon structure and reading frame.
Exon skipping does not mean full-length gene replacement.
Study 201 and its follow-up are not independent trial replications.

regulatory.status: Approved for ambulatory patients aged 4 years and older; 2025 indication restriction and liver-injury boxed warning

trials.name: EMBARK randomized year 1
trials.summary: Week-52 NSAA primary endpoint was not met: difference 0.65 points (95% CI −0.45 to 1.74; P=0.2441). Micro-dystrophin increased and some secondary outcomes favored treatment.

trials.name: EMBARK year 2 follow-up
trials.summary: Longer follow-up is reported separately from the randomized year-one analysis; it must not erase the original primary-endpoint result.

phenotypes.label: Muscle weakness
phenotypes.rationale: NSAA measures several motor skills; it is not a direct strength assay or a cardiomyopathy endpoint.

engaged: Skeletal muscle: micro-dystrophin expression
cells.notes: An engineered shortened transgene is used. Human muscle expression does not establish every clinical endpoint.

evidence.claim: EMBARK documented treatment-associated micro-dystrophin expression.
The randomized trial did not meet its prespecified motor-function primary endpoint.
Fatal liver injury reports led FDA to restrict the indication and add a boxed warning in November 2025.

conclusion.summary: Muscle molecular engagement and an approved indication coexist with a null pivotal primary endpoint and important safety restrictions.

limitations: Secondary and later analyses have different evidential status from the prespecified primary test.

trials.name: OASIS-HAE
trials.summary: 90 randomized; 80 mg every 4 weeks n=45, every 8 weeks n=23, placebo n=22. Attack rate per 4 weeks: 0.44, 1.02, 2.26; reduction 81% (95% CI 65–89) and 55% (22–74).

phenotypes.label: Angioedema
phenotypes.rationale: Clinical attacks directly assess the recurrent swelling phenotype in C1-INH HAE.

diseaseRelevant: Vascular permeability system affected by excess bradykinin
engaged: Reduced circulating prekallikrein
bypass: Suppress kallikrein–kinin pathway instead of repairing SERPING1
cells.notes: Attack reduction does not imply direct rescue of vascular endothelial subtypes.

evidence.claim: Randomized data show fewer confirmed HAE attacks.
Hepatic prekallikrein reduction changes a downstream pathway rather than correcting C1 inhibitor.

conclusion.summary: Supports systemic pathway suppression for C1-INH HAE attacks.

limitations: The pivotal population was HAE type I/II; other genetic HAE etiologies are not established subgroups.
Pediatric evidence includes seven participants and extrapolation.
assessments.geneRoleNotes: SERPING1 defines the studied C1-INH disease; KLKB1 is the target.

assessments.gene: LPL; APOC2; APOA5; GPIHBP1; LMF1 | target APOC3
assessments.disease: Familial chylomicronemia syndrome; current label also includes severe hypertriglyceridemia
assessments.modality: GalNAc-conjugated RNase H suppression of APOC3

regulatory.status: Approved adjunct to diet in adult FCS; current label also includes adult severe hypertriglyceridemia (not necessarily inherited).

trials.name: BALANCE
trials.summary: 66 genetically identified FCS patients randomized 80 mg/50 mg/placebo. Published 80-mg TG difference −43.5 percentage points (95% CI −69.1 to −17.9); 50-mg primary not significant. Pancreatitis episodes: 1 in each active group versus 11 placebo; pooled rate ratio 0.12 (0.02–0.66).

phenotypes.label: Hypertriglyceridemia
phenotypes.rationale: A direct biochemical phenotype; the approved FCS indication is triglyceride reduction.

phenotypes.label: Acute pancreatitis
phenotypes.rationale: A separate secondary clinical endpoint, pooled across active doses.

diseaseRelevant: LPL-mediated triglyceride clearance; pancreas injured during attacks
engaged: Reduced serum apoC-III and triglycerides
bypass: Reduce apoC-III-mediated inhibition of triglyceride clearance
cells.notes: The intervention suppresses a source protein; pancreas exposure is not required for pancreatitis reduction.

evidence.claim: The trial supports triglyceride reduction and fewer secondary pancreatitis episodes.
Source-protein suppression does not identify or repair a pancreatic cell subtype.
FCS has multiple genetic etiologies; gene arrays identify the disease family, not uniform representation or efficacy for every genotype in this product’s trial.

conclusion.summary: Supports lipid-pathway bypass; clinical pancreatitis and biochemical triglyceride evidence remain separate.

limitations: The 50-mg FCS primary comparison was not significant; the approved FCS dose is 80 mg.
2026 severe-hypertriglyceridemia trials are distinct from genetically identified FCS.
Primary publication and regulatory-label estimators have different confidence intervals.
assessments.geneRoleNotes: FCS is etiologically heterogeneous across the listed genes; APOC3 is a separate target. This is not proof of efficacy for each gene or allele.

assessments.gene: LPL; APOC2; APOA5; GPIHBP1; LMF1 | target APOC3
assessments.disease: Familial / persistent chylomicronemia, with or without a genetic diagnosis in PALISADE

regulatory.status: Approved adjunct to diet for triglyceride reduction in adult FCS.

trials.name: PALISADE
trials.summary: 75 randomized 25 mg/50 mg/placebo. Approved 25-mg arm n=26 versus placebo n=25: TG treatment difference −58.7 percentage points (95% CI −89.6 to −27.9). Published pooled pancreatitis odds ratio 0.17 (0.03–0.94).

phenotypes.label: Hypertriglyceridemia
phenotypes.rationale: Biochemical primary endpoint.

phenotypes.label: Acute pancreatitis
phenotypes.rationale: Secondary clinical endpoint pooled over two doses in the publication.

diseaseRelevant: LPL-mediated triglyceride clearance; pancreas injured during attacks
engaged: Reduced serum apoC-III and triglycerides
bypass: Reduce apoC-III-mediated inhibition of triglyceride clearance
cells.notes: The intervention suppresses a source protein; pancreas exposure is not required for pancreatitis reduction.

evidence.claim: Randomized data favor triglyceride reduction and pooled pancreatitis incidence.
Only 46% of the approved-dose arm and 56% of placebo had genetic confirmation; aggregate effects are not allele-specific.
FCS has multiple genetic etiologies; gene arrays identify the disease family, not uniform representation or efficacy for every genotype in this product’s trial.

conclusion.summary: Supports APOC3 pathway suppression; the broader clinical cohort cannot be treated as a single-gene efficacy experiment.

limitations: Current approved dose and published pooled-dose pancreatitis analysis differ.
Do not assume every trial participant had biallelic LPL-pathway disease.
assessments.geneRoleNotes: FCS is etiologically heterogeneous across the listed genes; APOC3 is a separate target. This is not proof of efficacy for each gene or allele.

assessments.gene: LPL; APOC2; APOA5; GPIHBP1; LMF1 | target APOC3
assessments.modality: Unconjugated RNase H antisense suppression of APOC3

regulatory.status: EU conditional authorization for adults with genetically confirmed FCS at high pancreatitis risk and inadequate diet/lipid-drug response.

trials.name: APPROACH
trials.summary: 66 randomized: month-3 TG change −77% versus +18%, p<0.001. 15/33 active patients developed platelets below 100,000/µL, including two below 25,000/µL.

phenotypes.label: Hypertriglyceridemia
phenotypes.rationale: Direct biochemical endpoint; long-term prevention of pancreatitis is separate.

diseaseRelevant: LPL-mediated triglyceride clearance; pancreas injured during attacks
engaged: Reduced serum apoC-III and triglycerides
bypass: Reduce apoC-III-mediated inhibition of triglyceride clearance
cells.notes: The intervention suppresses a source protein; pancreas exposure is not required for pancreatitis reduction.

evidence.claim: Randomized data show substantial triglyceride lowering.
Thrombocytopenia constrains the treatment; a positive lipid endpoint is not a complete benefit–risk conclusion.
FCS has multiple genetic etiologies; gene arrays identify the disease family, not uniform representation or efficacy for every genotype in this product’s trial.

conclusion.summary: Supports the APOC3 pathway effect with a material platelet-safety constraint.

limitations: EU conditional status and approved population differ from later APOC3 products.
Cross-trial lipid reductions do not establish comparative superiority.
assessments.geneRoleNotes: FCS is etiologically heterogeneous across the listed genes; APOC3 is a separate target. This is not proof of efficacy for each gene or allele.

regulatory.status: Approved for pediatric/adult SMA, including infants younger than 2 months; current label September 2026.

trials.name: FIREFISH Part 2
trials.summary: Open-label infantile SMA: 12/41 (29%) sat without support for at least 5 seconds after 12 months.

trials.name: SUNFISH Part 2
trials.summary: 180 randomized nonambulatory type 2/3 patients: month-12 MFM32 difference 1.55 points (95% CI 0.30–2.81), p=0.0156.

phenotypes.label: Muscle weakness
phenotypes.rationale: Motor performance measures consequences of weakness; these tasks do not isolate a causal cell subtype.

diseaseRelevant: Spinal motor neurons and neuromuscular system
exposed: Systemic tissues after oral treatment; CNS exposure supported nonclinically
engaged: Increased blood SMN protein; human motor-neuron-specific splice engagement not directly measured
bypass: Increase SMN2-derived SMN to compensate for SMN1 deficiency
cells.notes: Broad systemic delivery means trial benefit cannot identify a uniquely sufficient CNS cell target.

evidence.claim: Separate infantile and randomized later-onset studies support motor benefit.
Blood SMN and systemic exposure are not direct proof of isolated motor-neuron rescue.

conclusion.summary: Supports SMN2 compensation in SMA across studied populations.

limitations: Infantile FIREFISH is uncontrolled; SUNFISH includes nonambulatory patients age 2–25.
SMN2 is the target, not the disease-causing SMN1 locus.

regulatory.status: Approved September 3, 2026 for pediatric and adult Alexander disease.

trials.name: Pivotal Study 1
trials.summary: 49 randomized; primary stratum compared 50 mg (n=17) with shared controls (n=13). Week-61 gait-speed difference 33.3 percentage points (95% CI 1.44–65.25), p=0.041; changes −2.1% versus −35.4%.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Percent change in 10-meter-walk gait speed at week 61

phenotypes.label: Gait disturbance
phenotypes.rationale: Direct gait measure; primary analysis was restricted to the motor-impaired stratum.

exposed: CSF after intrathecal dosing; astrocyte exposure not directly measured in humans
engaged: Plasma GFAP 33.6% lower versus controls: an indirect target-engagement measure
cells.notes: Motor benefit and plasma GFAP lowering do not demonstrate cell-resolved human astrocyte rescue.

evidence.claim: The randomized primary analysis supports preservation of gait speed.
An astrocytopathy-targeted ASO does not establish uniquely sufficient astrocyte rescue from a plasma marker.

conclusion.summary: Supports GFAP lowering with motor benefit; direct human astrocyte rescue remains unresolved.

limitations: Small primary subgroup and broad confidence interval; age under 2 efficacy was extrapolated.
Some secondary global-impression endpoints were nonsignificant; aseptic meningitis is a labeled risk.

assessments.modality: Intravenous enzyme replacement with transferrin-receptor BBB shuttle

regulatory.status: Accelerated approval March 24, 2026: pediatric patients ≥5 kg before advanced neurologic impairment, based on CSF heparan-sulfate reduction; confirmatory clinical benefit remains required.

trials.name: Phase 1/2 Trial 1
trials.summary: 47 treated; 44 week-24 CSF measurements. Mean CSF heparan-sulfate reduction 91% (95% CI 89–92%). Uncontrolled adaptive behavior stabilized or improved; this is not randomized neurologic efficacy.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Registered primary outcomes concern safety and urine total GAG; CSF HS and adaptive behavior are distinct substrate/clinical assessments

phenotypes.label: Global developmental delay
phenotypes.endpoint: CSF heparan sulfate; exploratory adaptive behavior
phenotypes.rationale: CSF substrate is a proxy for neurological burden, not a direct developmental endpoint.

diseaseRelevant: CNS and peripheral lysosomal compartments with IDS deficiency
exposed: Systemic infusion; transferrin-receptor transport is intended to deliver enzyme across BBB
engaged: Reduced CSF and urine substrates; no human cell-resolved lysosomal engagement shown
bypass: Exogenous IDS replaces enzyme activity without correcting IDS DNA
cells.notes: TFRC is a delivery receptor; its expression does not alone identify the therapeutically rescued CNS cells.

evidence.claim: CSF substrate reduction supports pharmacodynamic activity.
The label states that substrate-change relationships to clinical response are not established.
TFRC denotes delivery-receptor identity, not the disease locus.

conclusion.summary: Supports substrate lowering and a delivery mechanism; clinical and cell-specific neurologic rescue remain unresolved.

limitations: Single-arm, heterogeneous prior-treatment cohort; CSF HS assay estimates selected disaccharides.
Confirmatory outcome and cell-specific rescue cannot be inferred from accelerated approval.

assessments.disease: 5q spinal muscular atrophy with ongoing SMN2-targeted treatment
assessments.modality: Monoclonal antibody inhibition of myostatin activation

regulatory.status: Approved September 11, 2026 for SMA age ≥2 years on an SMN2-targeted therapy; recommended 10 mg/kg every 4 weeks.

trials.name: SAPPHIRE / Study 1
trials.summary: 188 randomized nonambulatory patients on nusinersen/risdiplam. Prespecified pooled-dose primary age-2–12 analysis: HFMSE difference 1.8 (95% CI 0.30–3.32), p=0.019. Labeled 10-mg/kg analysis: 2.2 (0.49–3.95), nominal p=0.0121.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Change from baseline in HFMSE at 12 months in main efficacy population

phenotypes.label: Muscle weakness
phenotypes.rationale: Functional measure includes neuronal and muscle contributions; it does not isolate either cell compartment.

diseaseRelevant: Motor-neuron disease with downstream muscle weakness
exposed: Systemic antibody exposure; human muscle-cell-specific distribution not measured here
engaged: Serum latent-myostatin increases, consistent with binding proforms of myostatin
bypass: Muscle-directed myostatin pathway inhibition complements SMN restoration
cells.notes: MSTN is the downstream pharmacological target; the therapy neither repairs SMN1 nor establishes motor-neuron rescue.

evidence.claim: Randomized adjunct treatment improved the prespecified motor endpoint.
Benefit via a muscle-growth pathway cannot validate a claim that SMN1 correction occurred in motor neurons.

conclusion.summary: Supports adjunct motor benefit through a downstream muscle pathway; neuronal causal rescue remains unresolved.

limitations: Trial required background SMN2 therapy; efficacy of antibody monotherapy was not tested.
Main efficacy population age 2–12; higher dose added no efficacy; fractures are a labeled risk.

assessments.modality: Thyroid hormone analogue / receptor agonist bypassing MCT8 transport

regulatory.status: FDA approved September 28, 2026 and EU authorized February 12, 2025 for peripheral thyrotoxicosis in MCT8 deficiency; approval does not establish neurological rescue.

trials.name: ReTRIACt / Study 1
trials.summary: 20 enrolled, 15 randomized: 30-day withdrawal T3 rate ratio placebo/tiratricol 1.5 (95% CI 1.0–2.2), p=0.034. Rescue criterion: 4/8 placebo versus 1/7 tiratricol; proportion-difference CI −0.16 to 0.77 includes no difference.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Rate of serum total T3 change and proportion meeting biochemical rescue criterion over 30 days

trials.name: TRIAC I / Study 2
trials.summary: 46 treated, 45 analyzed: month-12 serum T3 323.4 to 118.3 ng/dL; mean change −205.2 (95% CI −235.7 to −174.6), with exploratory heart-rate reduction.

trials.name: TRIAC II 96-week primary analysis
trials.summary: Neurodevelopmental GMFM-88 and BSID-III gross-motor co-primary endpoints did not improve significantly versus prespecified historical-control thresholds despite T3 lowering. Long-term follow-up remains active.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: GMFM-88 and BSID-III gross-motor development at 96 weeks and later follow-up

phenotypes.label: Tachycardia
phenotypes.endpoint: Serum T3 and exploratory heart rate
phenotypes.rationale: Hormone lowering is a biochemical proxy; heart-rate signs are secondary clinical observations.

phenotypes.label: Global developmental delay
phenotypes.rationale: Developmental motor domains do not measure the full developmental phenotype.

diseaseRelevant: Brain thyroid-hormone insufficiency and systemic hormone excess
exposed: Systemic oral exposure; tiratricol enters cells independently of MCT8
engaged: Circulating T3 reduction; human neuronal receptor engagement not directly demonstrated
bypass: THR-beta agonism and thyroid-axis modulation bypass the deficient transporter
cells.notes: THRB is an agonist target, not the disease gene. Peripheral biochemical benefit must remain separate from neurological efficacy.

evidence.claim: Hormone lowering supports the approved peripheral indication.
TRIAC II did not establish its motor-development co-primary benefit.
T3 normalization cannot establish CNS or cell-specific rescue.

conclusion.summary: Supports peripheral biochemical benefit; studied neurological co-primary efficacy was not established.

limitations: Withdrawal trial was short and small; TRIAC I/II were uncontrolled.
T3 immunoassay interference requires LC-MS/MS; numerical development changes do not replace historical-control comparisons.

assessments.disease: Pompe disease, infantile-onset and late-onset populations

regulatory.status: Approved for Pompe disease; current US label includes infantile and late onset

trials.name: LOTS
trials.summary: 90 ambulatory patients over 78 weeks: published estimates favored treatment by 28.1 m in 6MWT (P=.03) and 3.4 percentage points in predicted FVC (P=.006). The current FDA label uses an analysis with FVC difference 3.4 points (95% CI 1.3–5.5; P=.004), while walking difference 28 m has CI −1 to 52 and P=.06; the walking significance is analysis-dependent.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Summary of Patients Reporting Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events; Mean Distance Walked as Measured by Six-minute Walk Test (6MWT) at Weeks 0 and 78, and Mean Change From Baseline; Percent of Predicted Forced Vital Capacity (FVC); Recombinant Human Acid Alpha-Glucosidase (rhGAA) Pharmacokinetic Parameters: Area Under the Curve (AUC); Recombinant Human Acid Alpha-Glucosidase (rhGAA) Pharmacokinetic Parameters: Mean Maximum Plasma Concentration(Cmax); Recombinant Human Acid Alpha-Glucosidase (rhGAA) Pharmacokinetic Parameters: Mean Time to Maximum Plasma Concentration(Tmax)

trials.name: Infantile-onset registration cohorts
trials.summary: The label reports 15/18 infants alive without invasive ventilation at age 18 months versus only 1/61 historical untreated infants alive. Motor development remained delayed in most, with regression in some; LV mass reduction did not correlate with ventilator-free survival.

phenotypes.label: Respiratory insufficiency
phenotypes.rationale: FVC is respiratory function and survival/ventilation is a composite; neither proves resolution of all respiratory manifestations.

phenotypes.label: Muscle weakness
phenotypes.rationale: Walking integrates strength, endurance and cardiopulmonary function; it is not a muscle-cell assay.

diseaseRelevant: Skeletal and respiratory muscle fibers; cardiomyocytes in infantile disease
engaged: Mannose-6-phosphate receptor-mediated lysosomal GAA uptake, label mechanism
cells.notes: Exogenous enzyme comes from manufacturing cells. Recipient-cell uptake is mechanistic; neither clinical trial establishes rescue of a uniquely necessary muscle subtype.

evidence.claim: Randomized FVC and published walking results support systemic GAA replacement in the enrolled late-onset population.
The regulatory walking analysis crosses the null; infant cohorts use historical controls and cardiac substrate changes do not establish equivalent motor rescue.
The label carries boxed hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis, immune-mediated reaction and acute cardiorespiratory-failure risks; CRIM status and antibody responses matter.

conclusion.summary: Supports GAA replacement and respiratory benefit; function does not resolve causal recipient-cell subtypes.

limitations: Historical infant controls differ from a randomized placebo comparison.
Enzyme uptake and disease stage can limit benefit; absence of full motor recovery does not identify an incorrect atlas cell prediction.

regulatory.status: Approved in US for late-onset Pompe age 1+; infantile-onset efficacy is not this US indication

trials.name: COMET
trials.summary: 100 treatment-naive patients: at week 49, predicted upright FVC difference 2.43 points (95% CI −0.13–4.99) versus alglucosidase. Noninferiority met (P=.0074); superiority failed (P=.063), stopping hierarchical testing. Walking difference 30.01 m favored avalglucosidase, but is secondary/nominal after the hierarchy stopped.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: PAP: Change From Baseline in Percent Predicted FVC in Upright Position at Week 49

phenotypes.label: Respiratory insufficiency
phenotypes.rationale: Measures pulmonary function rather than categorical resolution of respiratory insufficiency.

phenotypes.label: Muscle weakness
phenotypes.rationale: Composite functional endurance; secondary nominal comparison is not proof of muscle-cell rescue.

engaged: High-affinity M6P receptor uptake and lysosomal glycogen hydrolysis, label mechanism
cells.notes: Urinary Glc4 reduction is a glycogen-metabolism biomarker, not cell-subtype rescue or proof of superiority over every other enzyme.

evidence.claim: COMET establishes respiratory noninferiority to alglucosidase in treatment-naive late-onset disease.
The prespecified superiority test did not meet significance; favorable nominal walking results cannot replace that primary comparison.
Boxed anaphylaxis/hypersensitivity, infusion reactions and cardiorespiratory failure require product-specific monitoring.

conclusion.summary: Respiratory noninferiority with unresolved superiority; clinical outcomes do not validate a particular muscle-cell prediction.

limitations: Treatment-naive population and late-onset indication constrain extrapolation.
Improved receptor binding is not direct evidence of human cell-restricted causal rescue.

assessments.disease: Late-onset Pompe disease after insufficient response to enzyme replacement
assessments.modality: Intravenous GAA replacement plus circulating enzyme stabilizer

regulatory.status: Approved in US for adults weighing ≥40 kg who are not improving on current enzyme replacement; combination required

trials.name: PROPEL
trials.summary: 123 treated patients: primary walking superiority failed; published 52-week changes were +20.8 versus +7.2 m (difference 13.6 m, 95% CI −2.8–29.9). FDA label separately reports walking difference 14 m (CI −1–28) and sitting FVC difference 2.3 points (CI 0.02–4.62). ERT-experienced subgroup comparisons are nominal. The comparator was a non-US-approved alglucosidase product.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Change From Baseline to Week 52 in 6 Minute Walk Distance (6MWD)

phenotypes.label: Muscle weakness
phenotypes.rationale: Functional endurance integrates several tissues; superiority failed in the overall population.

phenotypes.label: Respiratory insufficiency
phenotypes.rationale: Secondary pulmonary-function endpoint; not a claim of full respiratory or cellular restoration.

exposed: Systemic circulation; miglustat given orally before IV enzyme
engaged: Cipaglucosidase M6P-mediated lysosomal uptake; miglustat stabilizes infused GAA in blood
cells.notes: Here miglustat protects the infused enzyme. This combination is distinct from miglustat used as substrate reduction for Gaucher disease; improved stability does not establish subtype-specific tissue delivery.

evidence.claim: Secondary respiratory and ERT-experienced subgroup results favor the combination under their stated analyses.
PROPEL did not show primary walking superiority in the overall population.
FDA explicitly limits comparative conclusions against a US-approved alglucosidase product; US use is restricted to ERT-experienced adults ≥40 kg.
Boxed hypersensitivity/infusion/cardiorespiratory risks and embryo-fetal toxicity restrictions apply to the combination.

conclusion.summary: Primary walking superiority was not demonstrated; selected respiratory evidence supports a bounded treatment strategy, with cell rescue unresolved.

limitations: Do not pool regulatory and publication analyses as independent trials.
Nominal subgroup findings do not establish benefit for treatment-naive patients or comparative superiority to all approved enzymes.

regulatory.status: EU approved for long-term replacement in confirmed Fabry disease; pediatric age 0–6 efficacy/dosing not established

trials.name: NIH placebo-controlled pain study
trials.summary: 26 adult males: BPI neuropathic pain severity declined from 6.2 to 4.3 with enzyme; placebo did not significantly change (between-group P=.02). Inulin clearance comparison was not significant (P=.19), although creatinine clearance favored treatment.

phenotypes.label: Pain
phenotypes.endpoint: Brief Pain Inventory neuropathic pain severity off pain medication
phenotypes.rationale: Direct pain severity assessment; the broader HPO Pain term does not assert every pain syndrome improved.

phenotypes.label: Renal insufficiency
phenotypes.rationale: Different renal-function measures gave different results; neither establishes prevention of end-stage kidney disease in this small trial.

diseaseRelevant: Renal glomerular/tubular cells; cardiomyocytes; peripheral sensory system
exposed: Systemic IV enzyme; multiple peripheral tissues
engaged: Human tissue substrate reductions in renal epithelial/endothelial cells and cardiomyocytes reported in EU label
cells.notes: Tissue Gb3 clearance is engagement, not restoration of neuronal function or evidence that one cell subtype causes clinical benefit.

evidence.claim: Placebo-controlled pain reduction supports clinical symptom benefit in the enrolled adult males.
Renal clearance measures diverged, and a small short trial cannot establish long-term event prevention.
EU label documents substrate reduction in several recipient-cell classes rather than a single tissue.
Infusion-associated reactions and anaphylaxis are reported; age 0–6 safety/efficacy is not established.

conclusion.summary: Supports pain relief and multi-tissue substrate clearance; causal cell specificity and long-term organ protection remain separate questions.

limitations: This is a distinct enzyme preparation and dose from agalsidase beta.
The pain endpoint does not demonstrate rescue of a particular sensory-neuron population.

regulatory.status: FDA traditional approval since March 11, 2021 conversion; confirmed Fabry disease age 2+

trials.name: Placebo-controlled endothelial substrate trial
trials.summary: 58 patients over 20 weeks: renal capillary GL-3 score zero in 20/29 treated versus 0/29 placebo patients (P<.001); biopsies also support heart and skin capillary endothelial clearance.

trials.name: Advanced Fabry clinical-event study
trials.summary: 82 adults: primary proteinuria-adjusted intention-to-treat clinical-event HR 0.47 (95% CI 0.21–1.03; P=.06). Protocol-adherent and ancillary subgroup analyses favored treatment, but did not replace the primary result. FDA label reports unadjusted HR 0.57 (CI 0.27–1.22).
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Number of Participants Experiencing a Clinically Significant Renal, Cardiac or Cerebrovascular Event and/or Death in Fabrazyme (Agalsidase Beta) Patients as Compared to Placebo Patients

phenotypes.label: Renal insufficiency
phenotypes.endpoint: Renal capillary GL-3 score and renal/cardiac/cerebrovascular/death composite
phenotypes.rationale: Substrate clearance is not kidney function; a multi-organ event composite cannot establish a kidney-specific rescue effect.

diseaseRelevant: Renal epithelial and vascular cells; cardiomyocytes; systemic endothelium
engaged: Human kidney, heart and skin capillary endothelial GL-3 clearance
cells.notes: Biopsy-defined engagement is stronger than exposure alone. Capillary endothelial clearance does not establish equivalent podocyte, cardiomyocyte or neuronal rescue.

evidence.claim: Randomized biopsy data demonstrate endothelial substrate clearance in human tissues.
The randomized advanced-disease primary clinical-event analysis did not reach significance despite favorable secondary analyses.
FDA conversion establishes current traditional status; it does not change the result of this particular randomized event trial.
Current label has boxed hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis and infusion-associated reaction precautions.

conclusion.summary: Strong human endothelial engagement with uncertain randomized major-event benefit in advanced disease; no uniquely causal cell-rescue inference.

limitations: Traditional conversion also reflects evidence beyond the two original trials; the corpus does not pool those designs.
Disease stage and irreversible tissue injury constrain extrapolation.

assessments.disease: Fabry disease with an amenable disease-causing GLA variant

regulatory.status: FDA ongoing accelerated approval in adults with amenable GLA variant; EU age 12+

trials.name: FACETS
trials.summary: Primary 6-month ≥50% kidney GL-3 response including amenable/non-amenable forms was 41% versus 28% (P=.30). In current FDA-label evaluable amenable patients, responders were 13/25 versus 9/20; baseline substrate burden influenced response. Non-amenable variants showed no kidney substrate change.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Percentage Of Participants With At Least A 50% Reduction From Baseline To Month 6 In The Average Number Of Kidney Interstitial Capillary (IC) Globotriaosylceramide (GL-3) Inclusions

trials.name: ATTRACT
trials.summary: 57 ERT-treated adults randomized to switch or continue ERT; four non-amenable cases excluded from primary efficacy analysis. Renal-function effects were comparable under prespecified criteria; major clinical events 29% versus 44% (P=.36), not a demonstrated event reduction.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Annualized Rate Of Change From Baseline To Month 18 In Measured Glomerular Filtration Rate; Annualized Rate Of Change From Baseline To Month 18 In eGFR

phenotypes.label: Renal insufficiency
phenotypes.endpoint: Kidney interstitial-capillary GL-3 and GFR trajectories
phenotypes.rationale: Histologic substrate and filtration measures have distinct meanings; neither proves long-term prevention of renal failure.

phenotypes.label: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
phenotypes.endpoint: Left ventricular mass index, secondary assessment
phenotypes.rationale: LV mass is an anatomic measure; it does not establish cardiac mortality reduction or identify causal cardiomyocyte rescue.

engaged: Mutant alpha-Gal A stabilization and lysosomal trafficking; HEK-293 amenability assay; kidney substrate assessment
cells.notes: An assay-amenable enzyme must retain activity. In-vitro responsiveness is not by itself pathogenicity or human organ rescue; the label explicitly notes benign GLA p.D313Y.

evidence.claim: Migalastat stabilizes selected residual-activity alpha-Gal A proteins and enables lysosomal trafficking.
FACETS did not meet its primary analysis including amenable and non-amenable forms; major-event superiority was not established in ATTRACT.
Only disease-causing amenable variants qualify; HEK-293 assay response alone is insufficient to diagnose Fabry disease. US approval remains accelerated.
Not recommended with eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m²; fasting/caffeine requirements affect exposure.

conclusion.summary: Allele-specific chaperoning is supported; primary and subgroup outcomes diverge and clinical confirmation remains required.

limitations: Do not treat all GLA loss variants as chaperone responsive.
The null full-population primary result does not refute responsiveness of an individually verified amenable pathogenic allele.
assessments.variantSpecificity: Amenable disease-causing GLA variant according to current label assay/table; exact allele and pathogenicity required.

assessments.disease: Type 1 and non-CNS manifestations of type 3 Gaucher disease

regulatory.status: Approved in adults and children for non-CNS manifestations of type 1 or type 3; type 3 added January 2026

trials.name: Randomized imiglucerase versus alglucerase
trials.summary: 30 patients: both preparations improved hematology and organ volumes with no significant between-product differences over 9 months. Current label at month 6 reports hemoglobin +1.9 versus +1.6 g/dL and spleen volume −35% versus −30%; these are active-comparator findings, not placebo effect estimates.

trials.name: Type 3 Gaucher registry evidence
trials.summary: The current label supports the non-CNS type 3 indication with observational registry hematology: hemoglobin change +1.8 g/dL in 117 patients and platelet increase 105×10³/mm³ in 116 patients near year 2. Timepoints were not prospectively fixed; no neurological efficacy endpoint is asserted.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: ICGG Gaucher Registry: To provide the Gaucher medical community with recommendations for monitoring patients and to provide reports on patient outcomes to help optimize patient care; Gaucher Pregnancy Sub-registry: To track pregnancy outcomes, including complications and infant growth, in all women with Gaucher disease during pregnancy, regardless of whether they receive disease-specific therapy, such as ERT with imiglucerase

phenotypes.label: Anemia
phenotypes.rationale: Measures anemia; correction can result from reduced splenic/marrow disease rather than gene correction in erythroid cells.

phenotypes.label: Thrombocytopenia
phenotypes.rationale: Direct hematologic measure; it does not demonstrate megakaryocyte-specific rescue.

phenotypes.label: Splenomegaly
phenotypes.rationale: Direct organ enlargement endpoint, distinct from neurological manifestations of type 3.

diseaseRelevant: Liver, spleen and marrow macrophages; CNS cells in neuronopathic disease
exposed: Systemic IV enzyme; mannose-dependent recipient-cell uptake
engaged: Label mechanism includes macrophage uptake and glucocerebroside hydrolysis
cells.notes: Manufactured enzyme is delivered to recipient cells. Improvement in anemia and platelets need not mean erythroid or platelet-lineage gene rescue. Current indication excludes CNS manifestations.

evidence.claim: Active-comparator trial and type 3 registry support non-CNS hematologic/visceral treatment under their distinct designs.
Mannose-mediated uptake includes macrophages, matching the storage-cell mechanism without proving unique causal sufficiency.
The 2026 label expansion covers non-CNS type 3 disease; it is not evidence of neurological rescue.
Current label has boxed hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis precautions.

conclusion.summary: Supports macrophage-directed replacement and non-CNS hematologic/visceral improvement; neuronal rescue remains unestablished.

limitations: Historical trials use the GBA gene name; typed locus uses current GBA1.
Registry improvement is not a randomized estimate and does not establish CNS benefit.

assessments.modality: Small-molecule glucosylceramide synthase inhibition / substrate reduction

regulatory.status: US adults with CYP2D6 extensive/intermediate/poor-metabolizer phenotype; EU also stable-on-ERT children age 6+ and ≥15 kg

trials.name: ENGAGE
trials.summary: 40 previously untreated adults: at 9 months spleen volume treatment difference −30.0% (95% CI −36.82 to −23.24); hemoglobin difference +1.2 g/dL and platelet difference +41.1% favored eliglustat. Clinical importance beyond these short-term endpoints remains bounded.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: PAP: Percent Change From Baseline in Spleen Volume (in Multiples of Normal [MN]) at Week 39 of the Primary Analysis Period With Eliglustat Tartrate Treatment as Compared to Placebo

trials.name: ENCORE
trials.summary: 160 stable ERT-treated adults randomized; per-protocol composite hematologic/organ-volume stability in 84/99 eliglustat versus 44/47 imiglucerase completers (difference −8.8%, 95% CI −17.6–4.2), meeting a 25% noninferiority margin. This demonstrates maintenance, not superior reversal.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Percentage of Participants Who Remained Stable for 52 Weeks During the Primary Analysis Period; Percentage of Participants Who Remained Stable Annually for 4 Years During the LTTP

phenotypes.label: Splenomegaly
phenotypes.rationale: Direct organ enlargement measure; it does not establish neurological or marrow-cell rescue.

phenotypes.label: Anemia
phenotypes.rationale: Direct anemia endpoint; downstream blood-cell effect does not identify the intervention cell.

phenotypes.label: Thrombocytopenia
phenotypes.rationale: Direct hematologic endpoint, separate from platelet-lineage gene correction.

diseaseRelevant: Reticuloendothelial macrophages in liver, spleen and marrow
engaged: Glucosylceramide synthase inhibition; systemic substrate reduction
bypass: Reduces substrate production rather than replaces GBA1
cells.notes: UGCG inhibition reduces synthesis upstream of the GBA1 degradation defect. Blood/organ outcomes do not establish macrophage subtype rescue or CNS efficacy.

evidence.claim: Randomized ENGAGE supports improvement in visceral and hematologic manifestations; ENCORE supports maintenance after ERT.
ENCORE used a broad 25% noninferiority margin and a completer/per-protocol analysis; it does not establish superiority.
CYP2D6 phenotype and CYP2D6/CYP3A interactions determine eligible exposure; high concentrations can prolong cardiac conduction intervals.

conclusion.summary: Supports substrate reduction for type 1 visceral/hematologic disease; clinical benefit does not isolate the target cell or correct GBA1.

limitations: CYP2D6 is a pharmacokinetic eligibility factor, not the Gaucher disease locus or therapeutic target.
No neuronopathic Gaucher efficacy is established here.
EU pediatric indication requires stable ERT and differs from US adult indication.
assessments.geneRoleNotes: GBA1 causes disease; UGCG encodes glucosylceramide synthase targeted by substrate reduction.

regulatory.status: Approved for non-CNS ASMD manifestations in adults and children

trials.name: ASCEND
trials.summary: Publication randomized 36 adults: 52-week DLCO relative change +22% versus +3.0% (P=.0004), spleen volume −39% versus +0.5% (P<.0001). Splenomegaly-related symptom score declined in both arms without separation (P=.64). FDA label efficacy set contains 31 patients and separately reports DLCO relative difference 20.9% and spleen volume difference −39.4%; denominators/analyses are kept separate.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Percent Predicted (% Predicted) Hemoglobin (Hb) and Altitude-Adjusted Diffusing Capacity of the Lung for Carbon Monoxide (DLco) at Baseline; Percent Change From Baseline in Percent Predicted (% Predicted) Hemoglobin (Hb) and Altitude-Adjusted Diffusing Capacity of the Lung for Carbon Monoxide (DLco) at Week 52; Combination Spleen Endpoint: Component 1: Spleen Volume (in MN) at Baseline; Combination Spleen Endpoint: Component 1: Percent Change From Baseline in Spleen Volume (in MN) at Week 52; Combination Spleen Endpoint (Primary for US Only): Component 2: Splenomegaly-Related Score (SRS) at Baseline; Combination Spleen Endpoint (Primary for US Only): Component 2: Change From Baseline in Splenomegaly-Related Score (SRS) at Week 52

phenotypes.label: Respiratory insufficiency
phenotypes.rationale: Gas-transfer function is clinically relevant but distinct from full respiratory symptom resolution; a relative % change is not a percentage-point change.

phenotypes.label: Splenomegaly
phenotypes.rationale: Anatomic enlargement improved while the associated symptom score did not show randomized separation.

diseaseRelevant: Peripheral storage cells in liver, spleen and lung; CNS cells in neuronopathic ASMD
engaged: Exogenous ASM and peripheral sphingomyelin clearance; human tissue evidence is not subtype-selective
cells.notes: Current label explicitly states olipudase is not expected to cross the blood-brain barrier or modulate CNS manifestations. Systemic benefit cannot be used to validate a neuronal rescue prediction.

evidence.claim: Randomized DLCO and organ-volume outcomes favor replacement in adult non-CNS ASMD.
The splenomegaly-related symptom score did not distinguish treatment from placebo; volume reduction does not guarantee symptom benefit.
Label excludes CNS efficacy and predicts lack of BBB access.
Boxed anaphylaxis risk; dose escalation, liver-transaminase monitoring and pregnancy restrictions address substrate mobilization and toxicity.

conclusion.summary: Lung-function and visceral benefit coexist with a neutral symptom score and inaccessible CNS disease; causal cell rescue is unresolved.

limitations: FDA and published efficacy sets have different denominators.
Pediatric efficacy extrapolation/open-label evidence is distinct from the adult randomized trial.

regulatory.status: Approved for perinatal/infantile- and juvenile-onset HPP; age of disease onset defines indication

trials.name: Infant treatment with extension and historical comparison
trials.summary: Published survival comparison pooled 37 treated versus 48 historical controls: 95% versus 42% alive at age 1 and 84% versus 27% at age 5. This uses NCT01205152 extension, NCT01176266 cohort and NCT01419028 natural history. Current label reports a larger 68-treated analysis with 97% versus 42% at age 1; these are different datasets.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Change in Rickets Severity From Baseline to Week 24, Based on Assessment of Skeletal Radiographs Using Radiologic Global Impression of Change (RGI-C)

phenotypes.label: Rickets
phenotypes.rationale: Radiographic skeletal improvement assesses the mineralization phenotype; it does not prove osteoblast gene rescue.

phenotypes.label: Respiratory insufficiency
phenotypes.rationale: Survival/ventilation can improve through rib/chest mineralization; it is not necessarily correction of primary lung or motor-neuron pathology.

exposed: Systemic subcutaneous protein with deca-aspartate bone-targeting domain
engaged: Extracellular pyrophosphate hydrolysis; bone-biopsy mineralization improvement
bypass: Supplies extracellular enzyme activity without gene correction of skeletal cells
cells.notes: The target includes extracellular bone substrate, not merely ALPL-expressing producer cells. Plasma substrate reductions did not correlate with clinical outcomes in the label.

evidence.claim: Survival and ventilation outcomes with skeletal mineralization improvements support enzyme replacement in severe early-onset HPP.
Survival estimates use historical controls rather than randomization; label and publication populations differ.
Plasma PPi/PLP reductions did not correlate with clinical outcomes; biochemical response cannot replace skeletal or functional assessment.

Boxed anaphylaxis; lipodystrophy, reported ectopic ocular/renal calcification and possible immune-mediated loss of response require monitoring. Causality of calcification versus underlying HPP is unresolved.

conclusion.summary: Supports mineralization and survival in early-onset disease; extracellular replacement can improve respiratory consequences without cell-specific genetic rescue.

limitations: Adults with childhood-onset HPP differ from adult-onset HPP, which is not this label indication.
Bone targeting and substrate depletion alone are not clinical efficacy endpoints.

assessments.disease: Congenital hemophilia A with or without FVIII inhibitors
assessments.modality: Bispecific antibody bypass of activated FVIII function

regulatory.status: Approved for routine prophylaxis, newborns and older, with/without inhibitors

trials.name: HAVEN 1, FVIII inhibitors
trials.summary: Randomized comparison: treated-bleed annualized rates 2.9 with emicizumab (35 patients) versus 23.3 without prophylaxis (18), an 87% reduction (P<.001).
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Model-Based Annualized Bleed Rate (ABR) for Treated Bleeds, Arm A: Emicizumab Versus Arm B: No Prophylaxis

trials.name: HAVEN 3, no FVIII inhibitors
trials.summary: 152 enrolled; randomized once-weekly and every-two-week groups had annualized treated-bleed rates 1.5 and 1.3 versus 38.2 without prophylaxis, reductions 96% and 97%. Prior factor-prophylaxis intraindividual comparison is a separate nonrandomized analysis.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Annualized Bleeding Rate (ABR) for Treated Bleeds

phenotypes.label: Abnormal bleeding
phenotypes.rationale: Measures clinical bleeding prevention, not production of normal FVIII.

phenotypes.label: Joint hemorrhage
phenotypes.rationale: Joint bleeding is distinct from reversal of established hemophilic arthropathy.

diseaseRelevant: FVIII-producing liver sinusoidal endothelial cells; injured tissues affected by bleeding
engaged: Bridges activated FIX and FX in extracellular coagulation
bypass: Antibody supplies FVIIIa-like cofactor function in circulation
cells.notes: Benefit requires neither restoration of endogenous F8 nor gene correction of its producer cells. This is a counterexample to inferring a causal tissue from therapy distribution.

evidence.claim: A primary human cell-sorting study found FVIII activity in liver sinusoidal endothelial cells, supporting an endogenous producer-cell context that differs from extracellular antibody bypass.
Randomized bleeding reduction supports downstream coagulation bypass with and without inhibitors.
Bridging circulating coagulation factors does not rescue F8-expressing cells or test their disease causality.
Boxed thrombosis/thrombotic microangiopathy risk when aPCC exposure averages >100 U/kg/24 h for ≥24 h; emicizumab also interferes with clotting assays.

conclusion.summary: Strong bleeding benefit via extracellular factor bypass; it cannot validate a particular F8 producer-cell prediction.

limitations: F9 and F10 are molecular binding targets, not hemophilia-A disease genes.
Comparator is no prophylaxis, not a randomized superiority comparison with every factor concentrate.
assessments.geneRoleNotes: F8 causes hemophilia A. Emicizumab binds activated FIX (F9) and FX (F10); it does not deliver or correct F8.

assessments.disease: Hereditary ATTR cardiomyopathy or early polyneuropathy; separate wild-type ATTR-CM population
assessments.modality: Small-molecule stabilization of extracellular TTR tetramers

regulatory.status: FDA adults with wild-type/hereditary ATTR-CM; EU formulation-specific CM and stage-1 symptomatic ATTR-PN indications

trials.name: ATTR-ACT cardiomyopathy
trials.summary: 441 adults, hereditary and wild-type combined: over 30 months death in 78/264 pooled tafamidis versus 76/177 placebo (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.51–0.96); cardiovascular hospitalization rate ratio 0.68. Walking and KCCQ decline were less with treatment. Pooled results are not an inherited-genotype-specific effect estimate.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Hierarchical Combination of All-Cause Mortality and Frequency of Cardiovascular-Related Hospitalizations

trials.name: Fx-005 Val30Met polyneuropathy
trials.summary: 125-patient ITT analysis did not meet coprimary outcomes: NIS-LL responders 45.3% versus 29.5% (P=.068); quality-of-life change 2.0 versus 7.2 (P=.116). Prespecified efficacy-evaluable analyses and secondary outcomes favored treatment; higher-than-anticipated liver-transplant dropout matters.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Percentage of Participants With Response to Treatment as Measured by Neuropathy Impairment Score - Lower Limb (NIS-LL) at Month 18; Change From Baseline in Norfolk Quality of Life- Diabetic Neuropathy (QOL-DN) Total Quality of Life (TQOL) Score at Month 18

phenotypes.label: Cardiomyopathy
phenotypes.endpoint: All-cause mortality and cardiovascular hospitalization ranked analysis
phenotypes.rationale: Clinically meaningful outcomes in ATTR-CM do not measure direct cardiomyocyte restoration or reverse all cardiac anatomy.

phenotypes.label: Peripheral neuropathy
phenotypes.endpoint: NIS-LL and Norfolk quality-of-life coprimary assessments
phenotypes.rationale: Neurologic and patient-reported peripheral-neuropathy outcomes; ITT coprimary comparisons were not significant.

diseaseRelevant: Peripheral nerves and cardiac tissue affected by extracellular amyloid
exposed: Systemic oral small molecule and circulating TTR
engaged: TTR tetramer stabilization in plasma; label pharmacodynamic assay
bypass: Slows extracellular amyloid precursor dissociation
cells.notes: Stabilizes the circulating precursor rather than correcting the TTR gene in its producers or directly rescuing cardiomyocytes/neurons. Plasma stabilization magnitude is not itself the clinical outcome.

evidence.claim: ATTR-ACT supports mortality, hospitalization and functional benefit in the combined ATTR-CM population.
The Val30Met polyneuropathy trial did not meet its ITT coprimary endpoints; evaluable-population benefit does not replace that result.
The label states clinical relevance of greater ex-vivo TTR stabilization is unknown.
Fetal-risk counseling and BCRP substrate interactions apply. EU CM evidence is limited in NYHA IV; formulation strengths/indications are not interchangeable per milligram.

conclusion.summary: Cardiomyopathy outcome benefit coexists with null ITT polyneuropathy coprimary comparisons; extracellular stabilization does not identify an affected-cell rescue mechanism.

limitations: Typed TTR disease-gene association applies to hereditary ATTR; wild-type ATTR is not an inherited TTR-variant disorder.
The current EU 61-mg film-coated tablet has a wild-type CM indication; capsules include hereditary CM.
assessments.geneRoleNotes: TTR is disease locus for hereditary subgroup and protein target; wild-type ATTR-CM is retained as a separate trial population.

assessments.disease: Cystic fibrosis with qualifying CFTR genotype
assessments.modality: Small-molecule CFTR correctors plus channel potentiator

regulatory.status: US age 2+ with clinical CF and ≥1 responsive or CFTR-protein-producing variant; indication revised March 2026

trials.name: F508del / minimal-function randomized trial
trials.summary: 403 patients age 12+: versus placebo, ppFEV1 difference 13.8 points at week 4 and 14.3 through week 24; pulmonary-exacerbation rate ratio 0.37 and sweat chloride difference −41.8 mmol/L. Sweat chloride is target engagement, not the clinical exacerbation endpoint.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Absolute Change in Percent Predicted Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 Second (ppFEV1)

trials.name: F508del-homozygous active comparison
trials.summary: 107 patients age 12+: at week 4, ppFEV1 difference +10.0 points versus tezacaftor/ivacaftor. Short active-controlled trial does not quantify long-term benefit for every genotype.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Absolute Change in Percent Predicted Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 Second (ppFEV1)

trials.name: Qualifying non-F508del randomized trial
trials.summary: Current label: 307 patients age 6+ without F508del but ≥1 qualifying responsive non-F508del allele; through week 24 ppFEV1 difference +9.2 points (95% CI 7.2–11.3), exacerbation rate ratio 0.28 (CI 0.15–0.51). This selected trial population does not test every protein-producing allele.
trials.registeredPrimaryEndpoint: Absolute Change in Percent Predicted Forced Expiratory Volume in 1 Second (ppFEV1)

phenotypes.label: Respiratory insufficiency
phenotypes.rationale: Measures airway function and clinical exacerbation frequency, not structural reversal of every pulmonary phenotype.

phenotypes.label: Bronchiectasis
phenotypes.rationale: FEV1/exacerbation improvement does not establish disappearance of bronchiectasis on imaging.

exposed: Systemic oral drugs; epithelial exposure is not cell-subtype-selective
engaged: CFTR trafficking/gating in assay cells; human sweat chloride response
cells.notes: Current label includes FRT single-variant assays and N1303K human bronchial epithelial experiments. These are model-cell functional assays, while sweat chloride is human epithelial engagement. Neither trial identifies a uniquely sufficient airway cell subtype.

evidence.claim: Randomized clinical trials demonstrate pulmonary benefit in the studied F508del and selected non-F508del populations.

Label eligibility is broader than alleles enrolled in trials; in-vitro chloride-response magnitude is not correlated with magnitude of clinical response. No rescue is inferred for alleles producing no target protein.
Corrector/potentiator mechanism and epithelial transport assays support CFTR functional restoration; cell-subtype attribution remains unresolved.

Current boxed warning includes drug-induced liver injury/failure, including transplantation/death; label also lists intracranial-hypertension, neuropsychiatric-event, CYP3A-interaction and cataract precautions.

conclusion.summary: Strong genotype-scoped clinical and epithelial engagement evidence; does not establish one causal airway-cell subtype or response of every eligible allele.

limitations: Exact genotype, target-protein availability and assay/clinical responsiveness remain distinct evidence questions.
Approval in age 2+ is not proof that every age/allele subgroup was directly randomized in these trials.
assessments.variantSpecificity: Current US label requires clinical CF plus ≥1 CFTR allele responsive by clinical/in-vitro data or producing CFTR protein; original pivotal genotypes and selected non-F508del trial remain separate.
